answer: A coating PUF protocol curbs Sybil attacks by measuring random capacitance variations across an opaque resin doped with dielectric pigment on each agent's chip. To harvest protocol reward nectar, an on-chip cipher encrypts digitized sensor readings into verifiable node credentials. An attacker incurs scarce silicon fabrication and custom packaging costs per identity. However, thermal drift and humidity can alter capacitance, causing false authentication rejections.
